title: All Hands: September 2026 - Company Update
summary: Monthly company all-hands: Alex opened with high level KPIs (ARR, usage growth), Priya covered product and infra milestones (Dedicated autoscale, KV cache improvements, quantization pipeline), Marco shared GTM highlights (enterprise deals, marketplace listings), Jasmine reviewed financials and runway, and Evan walked through roadmap priorities. Q&A covered SOC 2 timing, VPC/on-prem cadence, latency SLAs, and a request for clearer ownership of cross-team initiatives. Meeting ended with next steps and ask for volunteer leads for two initiatives.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-09-24
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Mitchell (CEO), Priya Desai (CTO), Samir Gupta (Head of Eng), Evan Park (Head of Product), Jasmine Li (CFO), Marco Alvarez (SVP Sales), plus company-wide attendees

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect): Monthly all-hands, highlights on revenue, product releases, compliance; Q&A at the end.

00:00 Alex Mitchell (CEO): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick note, we'll try to keep to 45 minutes and then q and a, um big thanks to everyone shipped a lot last quarter
00:18 Alex Mitchell (CEO): short rundown, revenue up 22% qoq, paid usage up 30% month-over-month, churn stable at 1.8 percent, big driver is improvements in Dedicated throughput and a couple of enterprise deals that closed in august
00:38 Jasmine Li (CFO): just to add, cash runway at 18 months post this quarter, we're on plan for the series C milestones, um minor ops expenses bumped due to region expansions but that's expected
01:05 Priya Desai (CTO): on the product side we shipped the initial autoscaling for Dedicated pools, still in early beta, it's already reducing cold-starts by about 35 percent in our internal load tests, there are caveats on burst throughput when quantized models are used
01:35 Samir Gupta (Head of Eng): yeah, that quantization note is important, our quant pipeline is moving fast but kernel selection still needs per-model tuning, sometime the quantized int8 path trades a little latency for cost savings, we're working on better heuristics
02:02 Evan Park (Head of Product): next up, product priorities: 1) Dedicated autoscale GA 2) KV cache improvements to reduce prefix latency 3) Console routing policies for cost-aware routing 4) Private deployment onboarding improvements including clearer network docs
02:30 Marco Alvarez (SVP Sales): on GTM, we listed on two marketplaces this quarter which helped inbound, closed three mid-market deals and one large enterp — enterprise partner with media analytics, they picked Dedicated with VPC and stricter audit logs
02:55 Alex Mitchell (CEO): good, quick shoutout to the infra team for reliability work, p99 across hosted APIs improved to 180ms on small prompts, still more to do on long-context performance
03:20 Jasmine Li (CFO): finance ask: if you're owning new region spend please coordinate with finance, invoices shifted a bit this quarter and we want to keep forecasting clean, also we'll share updated ARR deck later today
03:45 Priya Desai (CTO): on security/compliance, SOC 2 Type 1 in progress, we expect Type 2 by mid next year — timeline is estimate but we're prioritizing audit readiness for Private customers, SSO/SAML and RBAC are on track for the next release
04:12 Alex Mitchell (CEO): question about data residency — we have customers asking for EU-only data; plan is to support region-specific retention controls, that ties to the Private roadmap too
04:30 Audience Question (via chat): what about on-prem delivery for highly regulated customers?
04:38 Priya Desai (CTO): we've got an on-prem package in trial with one customer, it's essentially the private control plane with an on-prem runtime, main lift is networking and KMS integration, needs some docs and hardened install scripts
05:00 Samir Gupta (Head of Eng): engineering heads-up: we'll need two cross-functional sprints to harden the installer and expand E2E tests, volunteer leads please reach out after the meeting
05:20 Alex Mitchell (CEO): hiring update — we're green on hiring for Q4 but focus on infra, s-reliability, and sales engineers, recruiting numbers look healthy
05:40 Marco Alvarez (SVP Sales): enablement note: we'll update the sales playbook with the new Dedicated autoscale story — expect a playbook email and training session next week
06:05 Evan Park (Head of Product): roadmap deep-dive, kv cache changes: moving to a hybrid prefix/kv scheme that should cut repeated prefix token generation by up to 40 percent for chat-heavy apps, also we're adding cache invalidation hooks for streaming flows
06:45 Priya Desai (CTO): behind the scenes, kernel selection improvements are in A/B — picking kernels by seq-len distributions and hardware is reducing CPU spillovers on multicard configs
07:10 Alex Mitchell (CEO): product-market fit check: we still see strongest traction for companies building chat and document search, but embeddings-heavy analytics is catching up, cost optimizations are making embedding workflows cheaper
07:35 Audience comment: can we get a one-pager on recommended model/quant profiles for embeddings?
07:45 Evan Park (Head of Product): yes, we'll publish that, plus suggested batch sizes and latency tradeoffs
08:05 Jasmine Li (CFO): a quick finance FAQ, we'll be changing invoicing cadence for some regionals, more details in tomorrow's finance office hours, please review before the end of the month
08:28 Alex Mitchell (CEO): OK now Q&A live — please use raise-hand, i'll call on folks
08:40 Employee Question (Senior SE): what are the SLA targets for Dedicated vs Hosted?
08:48 Priya Desai (CTO): Hosted has a best-effort low latency goal, Dedicated SLA will be defined for reserved pools — target is 99.9 uptime and p95 latency targets per-config, but we need to codify numbers and offer clear SLO docs
09:22 Employee follow-up: any blockers for SOC 2?
09:30 Priya Desai (CTO): main blockers are evidence collection and a few remaining policy gaps, security team is running through control mapping this week, expect a SOC 2 roadmap doc from me next week
09:52 Employee: on Private deployments, who is the product owner?
10:00 Evan Park (Head of Product): i'm the product owner for Private but it's cross-functional; Samir will own the install/hardening work, Taylor will own customer onboarding and success docs
10:20 Taylor Chen (VP Customer Success): yes, and support will track requests in the new Private deployment tag in Zendesk, we'll aggregate common issues and publish the FAQ
10:40 Audience comment: can we have a public-facing status page for region incidents?
10:48 Samir Gupta (Head of Eng): we're working on a region-aware status page, it's in experimental, hope to roll next month, will include infra metrics and incident postmortems limited to what's safe to share
11:05 Employee (Product Designer): roadmap ask: will design resources be available for the Console revamp?
11:12 Evan Park (Head of Product): yes, we've allocated two designers for Q4, please submit briefs to the design backlog
11:30 Alex Mitchell (CEO): quick company note — partnership with a major cloud infra partner is moving to pilot; can't share partner name yet but it will help with private deployments and marketplace distribution
11:48 Marco Alvarez (SVP Sales): operationally, sales engineering playbooks will include benchmark scripts and a shared benchmark spreadsheet, SEs please check the Drive folder after this meeting
12:05 Alex Mitchell (CEO): ok closing notes: exec team will hold a follow-up across the cross-functional leads, we'll send calendar invites; appreciate the energy and shipping cadence
12:22 Audience applause (virtual chat)
12:30 Alex Mitchell (CEO): all right that wraps it up, thanks everyone, meeting end

Notes about transcript: transcription is imperfect — names and acronyms sometimes mistranscribed, times approximate. Shared artifacts referenced during the call: Confluence ARR deck (link posted in chat), Dedicated autoscale runbook (internal draft), KV cache tech brief (draft), marketplace listing screenshots (drive link).
notes: Artifacts: ARR deck (Confluence), Dedicated runbook (internal), KV cache brief (Drive). Volunteers requested for installer hardening and SOC2 evidence collection.
